correctness.rationale: For nonconstant binary words, one position cannot cover both singleton letter types. When fewer than four binary digram types appear, two positions suffice by explicit run/boundary cases. When all four appear, two positions must use one of two disjoint adjacent-digram pairings: witnessed respectively by both 001 and 110, or by both 100 and 011. Avoiding each pairing while retaining all digrams forces exactly two complementary alternating-interior families, each admitting a three-position construction. Direct composition counting proves the bivariate rational generating function. The standalone incidence-mask verifier independently checks every nonempty binary word of lengths 1–15 (65,534 total) and the closed coefficient formula through 299; finite tests are not treated as infinite proof.

value.rationale: The natural two-attractor optimization problem is known NP-complete over unrestricted alphabets, motivating the smallest nontrivial fixed-alphabet boundary. The claim resolves every binary instance structurally, not merely numerically: it characterizes the entire exceptional language, yields a uniform size bound three, determines exact length/weight enumerators and proves that three-mark instances have exponentially vanishing density. These are all-length, composition-sensitive structural consequences not implied by a generic decision algorithm or the distinct sharp-two edge-cover reduction.
